study_identification_part.si4_title: Alzheimer's disease heterogeneity revealed by neuroanatomical normative modeling

cm1_research_objectives.reason: Objectives are explicitly listed in the introduction. They state applying neuroanatomical normative modeling to a real-world AD cohort and outline three aims: assess intragroup heterogeneity, explore anatomo-clinical correlations, and examine the association between amyloid burden and cortical thickness deviations.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "The objectives of the current study were to (1) assess intragroup neuroanatomical heterogeneity in a real-world clinical cohort of patients with confirmed AD; (2) explore anatomo-clinical correlations at an individual level; (3) examine the association between global amyloid burden and deviations in cortical thickness."

A local adaptation dataset of 20 cognitively normal adults is described. However, explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria and QC standards for the local reference sample are not detailed beyond being CN adults scanned for research purposes; image quality criteria for the reference cohort rely on prior publications. Final sample sizes are reported.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The reference cohort consisted of a group of 33,072 cognitively normal adults pooled from publicly available neuroimaging datasets under a previous study" ... nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex are explicitly included as covariates in the normative model. Multi-site/scanner effects are addressed via hierarchical Bayesian regression and adaptation (transfer learning) using site-matched controls.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "...using age and sex as the covariates to index population variability in cortical thickness across all 148 regions of interest (ROIs)... This model was then optimized using cortical thickness data from controls scanned at the same acquisition site as the clinical cohort (n = 20). This gives stable estimates of the transferred model parameters in an adapted transfer learning approach."
